newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices fall further in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices fall further in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices continued to fall at auction sales in Sydney and Geelong this week, the Australian Council of wool Exporters said.
The eastern market indicator fell 24 cents to 550 cents a kg clean. A total of 64,277 bales were offered, with 15.5 percent passed in.
The council said that despite the smaller national offering, wool prices continued to fall.
"Demand from European processors continue to be very weak," the council said.
The council said exporters attributed some of this week's price falls to poor marketing strategies by wool growers and brokers.

Exporters report that some European processors are not renewing orders for purchases once existing orders have been completed. European sources report that retail sales of woolen garments have been poor recently.
In the futures market, a total of 324 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended October 3.
Sales next week are in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle with 115,694 bales on offer. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
